name: 0xdbdd45150249e229eB4c
archetype: In-play multi-sport taker (soccer goals, quiet books)
headline: Takes liquidity during live games across soccer, tennis, US sports and esports. It makes its money in soccer, typically buying Over on totals shortly after a goal and trading into quiet order books; several public rules pick out its trades, but none of them makes money held out.
mechanism: All sampled fills are taker fills; median fill about $11. US-league fills lose (-0.75%; spreads -8.4%); everything outside the US leagues earns +$59.8k on $1.32M (+4.5%). In soccer totals, 26% of its buys fall within 60 s after an ESPN goal wall clock (other takers 10%) and 96% of those are Over. It also trades disproportionately when the book has been quiet for 10 s or more.

roc.detail: 185%/month: 30-day PnL $61,712 on peak capital at risk $33,408; counting the on-chain collateral too ($244,193), at least 22%/month

onchain.detail: 200/200 sampled fills confirmed in Polygon OrderFilled events; 0% maker fills (95% CI 0%-2%), 0% of USDC

match.detail: US leagues (ESPN REACT): direction 59% vs 55% for other takers (perm p=0.005), no excess reaction (p=0.30). Reviewer rules: soccer Over after an ESPN goal hit 38% vs 11% (p=0.001); spreads lagging the moneyline matched on 141 fresh games (p=0.001). Real but narrow signatures

backtest.detail: REACT(D=10 s, W=120 s) held out +4.6% (47,819 trades, p(profit)=0.25); reviewer rules: soccer goal-react -12.3% (p=0.82), spreads-lag -3.4% to -6.2% on fresh games, win-probability gap +10.1% (p=0.13, five games give all of it); wallet's own fills +8.2% (p=0.19)

replicable.detail: speed is not the binding constraint, but no public rule reproduces its choice of line and price after a goal, so there is nothing to replicate

persistence.detail: last 30 days p=0.011; decline vs earlier p=0.15; last 15 vs prior 15 p=0.65; trend p=0.80. Its last three 30-day blocks were $62k, $24k and $22k after $184k, $237k and $143k; the tests do not call the decline significant, but two of the last three months were below $50k.

reasons: Several public rules identify slices of its trading, but none reproduces most of its decisions.
No rule that matches it is profitable on held-out or fresh games.
corrections: The earlier reason 'most of its volume has no public timestamped event feed' is wrong for soccer: ESPN's soccer API publishes goal times, and soccer is where it profits.
The original ESPN test covered only US leagues, which is its losing segment.
